o: She has lived here since 2020.
She lives here since 2020.
She is living here since 2020.
She have lived here since 2020.
questions.e: Use “has lived” with “since” for an action that began in the past and continues.

o: If it will rain, we stay inside.
If it rains, we will stay inside.
If it rains, we stayed inside.
If it rained, we will stay inside.
questions.e: After “if” for a real future possibility, use the present: “if it rains”.

o: They played when the bell was ringing yesterday.
They were play when the bell rang.
They were playing when the bell rang.
They was playing when the bell rang.
questions.e: Use the past continuous for the ongoing action and the past simple for the event.

o: He use to walked to school.
He was used walk to school.
He used walking to school.
He used to walk to school.
questions.e: Use “used to” plus the base form for a past habit.

o: We have already eaten lunch.
We has already ate lunch.
We already have eat lunch.
We have already eat lunch.
questions.e: After “have”, use the past participle: “eaten”.

o: Awa is more tall than Mariama.
Awa is taller than Mariama.
Awa is tallest than Mariama.
Awa is as taller than Mariama.
questions.e: For a short adjective, use “-er than”.

o: You should to drink more water.
You should drinking more water.
You should drink more water.
You should drank more water.
questions.e: After “should”, use the base verb without “to”.

o: There is too many people in the room.
There are too much people in the room.
There be too many people in the room.
There are too many people in the room.
questions.e: Use “are” with plural “people” and “many” with countable nouns.

o: I have never visited Dakar.
I never have visit Dakar.
I has never visited Dakar.
I have never visit Dakar.
questions.e: Use “have + past participle” for the present perfect.

o: The letters was sent yesterday.
The letters were sent yesterday.
The letters sent yesterday by him.
The letters were send yesterday.
questions.e: In the passive past, use “were + past participle” for plural “letters”.

o: She enjoys to read after class.
She enjoy reading after class.
She enjoys reading after class.
She enjoys read after class.
questions.e: After “enjoy”, use a verb ending in “-ing”.

o: We arrived to the station on time.
We arrive at the station last night.
We arrived in the station on time.
We arrived at the station on time.
questions.e: Use “arrive at” for a specific place such as a station.

o: I was cooking while my brother was studying.
I cooked while my brother study.
I was cooking while my brother studying.
I were cooking while my brother was studying.
questions.e: Use “was/were + -ing” for two actions happening at the same time.

o: She works here since three years.
She has worked here for three years.
She have worked here for three years.
She has work here for three years.
questions.e: Use “for” with a length of time and “has worked”.

o: This is the more interesting book in the library.
This is the interestingest book in the library.
This is the most interesting book in the library.
This is most the interesting book in the library.
questions.e: For a long adjective, use “the most” to form the superlative.

o: You must to wear a helmet when you ride.
You must wearing a helmet when you ride.
You must wore a helmet when you ride.
You must wear a helmet when you ride.
questions.e: After “must”, use the base form of the verb.

o: Although it was late, they continued working.
Although it was late, but they continued working.
Although it late, they continued working.
Despite it was late, they continued working.
questions.e: Use “although” without adding “but” in the same clause.

o: He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where I live yesterday.
He asked me where do I lived.
questions.e: In a reported question, use statement word order: “where I lived”.

o: The food is prepared now by them being.
The food are being prepared now.
The food is being prepared now.
The food is been prepared now.
questions.e: For an action happening now in the passive, use “is being + past participle”.

o: Neither answer are correct.
Neither answers is correct.
Neither answer be correct.
Neither answer is correct.
questions.e: “Neither” is singular here, so use “is”.

o: She is interested in learning English.
She is interested to learn English.
She is interested for learning English.
She interested in learn English.
questions.e: After “interested in”, use a noun or an “-ing” form.

o: We will meet after the lesson will end.
We will meet after the lesson ends.
We meet after the lesson ended tomorrow.
We will meet after the lesson ending.
questions.e: After “after” for a future event, use the present simple.

o: There were a lot of noise outside.
There was many noise outside.
There was a lot of noise outside.
There be a lot noise outside.
questions.e: “Noise” is uncountable, so use “a lot of” and singular “was”.

o: If I have more time, I would learned Wolof.
If I had more time, I will learned Wolof.
If I would have more time, I learned Wolof.
If I had more time, I would learn Wolof.
questions.e: For an unreal present situation, use “if + past” and “would + base verb”.
